capabilityNamingRule: A value named for a domain claims the domain migrated; a value named for a slice claims only the slice. Nothing may be named for a booking WRITE while POST /api/v1/bookings does not exist. Any NEW booking* capability must be added to an explicit allow-list in test/core/network/canonical_availability_test.dart. TAB 11: nothing may be named for a domain containing surfaces this CLIENT cannot call ('finance' would claim provider earnings and admin reconciliation). TAB 12: booking-experiences now spans FOUR capabilities, so no value may be named for that domain either.
absenceTaxonomy: THREE kinds, three treatments. (1) LEGACY lacks it - reschedule, refunds, disputes - report via a supports... flag. (2) CANONICAL lacks it - DELETE /api/user/notifications/:key - absent from the canonical source, repository calls compatibility directly. (3) THIS ACTOR may never call it - additionalWork.create - absent from the interface altogether, no method and no flag, because a flag implies a deploy that would turn it on and none will.
vocabularyRule: Where the backend SERVES its own vocabulary, consume it; where it does not, mirror and say so. Disputes return `categories` on every read (outside any branch), so DisputeCategory is an extension type over String. Reschedule reasons and refund triggers had no such endpoint and are mirrored enums.
